paragraphs.title: Hannah’s Prayer: The Lord’s Salvation and the Reversal of Fortunes

easy.explanation: Hannah says, “My heart rejoiceth in the Lord.”
The verse says, “The bows of the mighty men are broken.”
easy.q: What happens to the bows of the mighty men?

easy.explanation: The Lord raises the poor from the dust and lifts up the beggar.
easy.q: Who raises the poor from the dust?

answers: The full hire themselves for bread, and the hungry cease
The hungry become servants of the full
medium.explanation: The full hire themselves for bread, while the hungry cease.
medium.q: What happens to those who were full and those who were hungry?

medium.explanation: The phrase means became weak or diminished in strength.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “waxed feeble” mean?

medium.explanation: The verse says that by Him actions are weighed.
medium.q: Why does Hannah call the Lord “a God of knowledge”?

challenge.explanation: The Lord breaks the mighty, strengthens the weak, and lifts up the lowly.
challenge.q: What central theme appears throughout Hannah’s prayer?

answers: Human strength alone does not determine success
People always succeed by their own power
challenge.explanation: The verse teaches that human strength alone cannot secure victory.
challenge.q: What does “by strength shall no man prevail” teach?

answers: Give strength to the king and exalt the horn of His anointed
challenge.explanation: The Lord will give strength to His king and exalt the horn of His anointed.
challenge.q: What will the Lord do for His king and anointed?

paragraphs.title: Samuel amid the Corruption of Eli’s Sons

easy.explanation: Samuel ministered unto the Lord before Eli the priest.
The KJV calls them “sons of Belial.”
He carried a fleshhook of three teeth in his hand.
easy.q: What tool did the priest’s servant carry?

medium.explanation: They demanded flesh to roast before the fat was burned.
medium.q: What did Eli’s sons demand before the fat was burned?

medium.explanation: The expression describes men who were wicked and ungodly.
medium.q: What does “sons of Belial” mean in this context?

answers: Men abhorred the offering of the Lord
They refused to wear an ephod
medium.explanation: Their conduct caused people to abhor the Lord’s offering.
medium.q: Why was the sin of the young men very great?

answers: Samuel ministered before the Lord, but they did not know the Lord
Samuel was rich, but they were poor
Samuel was a king, but they were servants
challenge.explanation: Samuel served the Lord, while Eli’s sons did not know Him.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between Samuel and Eli’s sons?

answers: They were satisfied with their portion
They were willing to use coercion
challenge.explanation: Their words show that they intended to seize the offering by force.
challenge.q: What does “I will take it by force” reveal about Eli’s sons?

challenge.explanation: Their behavior treated the Lord’s offering with contempt.
challenge.q: What religious principle did their actions violate?

paragraphs.title: Samuel Grows and Eli Blesses Hannah’s Family

easy.explanation: Samuel was girded with a linen ephod.
easy.q: What was Samuel wearing as he ministered?

easy.explanation: His mother made him a little coat and brought it yearly.
easy.q: What did Hannah bring Samuel each year?

easy.explanation: The KJV says Hannah bare three sons and two daughters.
easy.q: How many sons and daughters did Hannah later have?

medium.explanation: Eli prayed, “The Lord give thee seed of this woman.”
medium.q: What did Eli ask the Lord to give Elkanah and Hannah?

answers: The Lord remembered her and gave her children
medium.explanation: The context explains that she conceived and bore children.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “the Lord visited Hannah” mean?

answers: The Lord visited Hannah and she had more children
medium.explanation: After the blessing, Hannah conceived and bore three sons and two daughters.

answers: Samuel turned away from the Lord
challenge.explanation: The passage says that the child Samuel grew before the Lord.
challenge.q: What relationship with the Lord is emphasized at the end of the passage?

answers: She continued caring for him while he served
She wanted him away from the sanctuary
challenge.explanation: Her yearly visits and gift show her continuing care for Samuel.
challenge.q: What does Hannah’s yearly gift show?

answers: Hannah had children, Eli blessed her, then Samuel grew
Eli blessed them, the Lord visited Hannah, and Samuel grew
Samuel grew, Eli blessed them, then Hannah married
challenge.explanation: That is the order given in the verses.

easy.explanation: Eli heard of all the evil his sons did unto Israel.
easy.q: What did Eli hear about his sons?

answers: The women that assembled at the door of the tabernacle
easy.explanation: The passage mentions women at the door of the tabernacle.
easy.q: Who was involved in the sinful behavior mentioned by Eli?

answers: He grew and was in favor
He was angry with the people
easy.explanation: Samuel grew and was in favor with the Lord and with men.

answers: He heard of their evil dealings
They failed to bring him a coat
They wanted to serve the Lord
medium.explanation: Eli said he had heard of their evil dealings from all the people.
medium.q: Why did Eli rebuke his sons?

answers: They caused the people to sin
They moved the people to another city
medium.explanation: Eli accused them of leading the Lord’s people into wrongdoing.
medium.q: What does “ye make the Lord’s people to transgress” mean?

medium.explanation: The text says they did not listen to their father’s voice.
medium.q: How did Eli’s sons respond to their father’s rebuke?

answers: They did evil, while Samuel grew and was in favor
They served faithfully, while Samuel stole
They were young, while Samuel was old
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts their evil conduct with Samuel’s good reputation.
challenge.q: What contrast is made between Eli’s sons and Samuel?

answers: They rejected the rebuke and did not change
challenge.explanation: Their refusal shows that they did not respond to Eli’s correction.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the sons’ refusal to listen?

challenge.explanation: The KJV says he was in favor both with the Lord and with men.
challenge.q: With whom was Samuel in favor?

paragraphs.title: The Accusation against Eli’s House and the Loss of Its Promise

easy.explanation: A man of God came unto Eli with the Lord’s message.
easy.q: Who came to Eli to rebuke him?

answers: Priestly service and the offerings made by fire
easy.explanation: The Lord chose Aaron’s house to serve as priests and receive the offerings.
easy.q: What did the Lord give the house of Aaron?

easy.explanation: The Lord accused Eli of honoring his sons above Him.
easy.q: Whom did Eli honor above the Lord?

answers: They dishonored the sacrifices and honored the sons above God
They refused to build the tabernacle
medium.explanation: The accusation concerned their treatment of the Lord’s offerings and their preference for Eli’s sons.

answers: Why do you despise and reject it?
Why do you lift it up?
medium.explanation: The phrase is figurative for treating the sacrifice with contempt.
medium.q: What does “kick ye at my sacrifice” mean?

answers: Those who honor the Lord will be honored
medium.explanation: The Lord says, “Them that honour me I will honour.”
medium.q: What principle appears at the end of the Lord’s message?

answers: His privileges did not excuse his abuse of the offerings
His privileges made him unable to sin
challenge.explanation: Although his house received sacred privileges, it remained accountable for dishonoring them.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between Eli’s privileges and his punishment?

answers: The promise of enduring priestly service was withdrawn because of sin
Eli’s house immediately left the tabernacle
challenge.explanation: The Lord withdrew the promise because they dishonored Him.
challenge.q: What does the withdrawal of the promise that Eli’s house would walk before the Lord forever mean?

answers: Honoring the sons above God leads to Eli’s house being lightly esteemed
challenge.explanation: Their dishonor of God results in their own being lightly esteemed.
challenge.q: What cause and effect appears in the Lord’s words?

paragraphs.title: Punishment for Eli’s House and the Faithful Priest

answers: They will both die in one day
easy.explanation: The Lord says that Hophni and Phinehas will both die in one day.
easy.q: What will happen to Eli’s two sons?

easy.explanation: The Lord says, “I will raise me up a faithful priest.”
easy.q: What will the Lord raise up?

easy.explanation: They will ask to be put into one of the priests’ offices for bread.
easy.q: What will the remnant of Eli’s house ask for?

medium.explanation: The Lord says He will cut off Eli’s arm and the arm of his father’s house.
medium.q: What loss will come upon Eli’s house?

medium.explanation: The arm represents strength and authority.
medium.q: In context, what does “cut off thine arm” symbolize?

medium.explanation: He is explicitly called a faithful priest.
medium.q: What quality will characterize the priest raised up by the Lord?

answers: Eli’s house will lose power, while the faithful priest will have a sure house
Eli’s house will be established, while the faithful priest will die
challenge.explanation: The Lord contrasts the fall of Eli’s house with the establishment of a faithful priest.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between Eli’s house and the faithful priest?

answers: They will fall from priestly privilege into dependence and need
challenge.explanation: Their request shows severe loss of status and material security.
challenge.q: What does the request for a piece of bread reveal about Eli’s descendants?

answers: Hophni and Phinehas will die in one day
challenge.explanation: The deaths of Eli’s two sons are given as the sign.
challenge.q: What is the immediate sign of the coming judgment?
